Carried; the row verdict (ea9371b) still ends with 'passes every drive gate at mu 0.15 on BOTH stages'. The design's headline advantage ('passes every drive gate at mu 0.15 on BOTH stages ... the first desmo-family drive that does', row verdict) rests on a gate the screener re-read for this design. Stage 1 is read on the built blended groove: the cap (back-drive) side is gated only outside the blend, and the blend spans K 0 to 10.72 deg of the 46.5 deg stroke. Inside it the built cap-side pressure angle is above the family gate 34.47 (43 - atan 0.15) from K 0 to 9.0 deg, above 60 deg to K 3.14, and above the self-locking line 81.47 (90 - atan 0.15) only to K 0.33. So the 'dwell lock' the reading exempts is real for the first 0.33 deg; from 0.33 to 9.0 deg the back-drive is not locked, it runs at 34.5-80 deg, ungated. The rest pose (dK 4.6, cap PA ~52.7) and the taken overhead pose at axial -135 (dK 5.8, ~47) sit in that band. No blended groove can pass a 43 - atan(mu) back-drive gate next to its dwell (the cap angle goes to 90 as the law's slope goes to 0), so the linear read's 35.05 at K 0 is itself an artefact of the law's kink: neither reading measures whether the wearer feels the 35-81 deg back-drive in the first 9 deg of K. Under the family's linear reading, the same claim placement has the cap side at 35.05 deg at K 0 against the mu 0.15 gate of 34.47 and fails at K 0 (fast 86.52); it passes at mu 0.135 (gate 35.31, fast 13.31), so its linear-read friction limit is mu ~0.139 (tan(43 - 35.05)), the same as desmo-slipper's measured jam at mu 0.14. The score does not move: fast 13.31 at mu 0.087 or 0.135 on the linear read equals the claim (docs/alignment/remeasure/desmo-conecut-knuckle-3r_s1read_check.json; docs/concepts/verify/desmo-conecut-knuckle-3r_v_probe_fast.json). The genuine gain is stage 2: the inverted slot keeps its PA stroke 64.5 deg of K up to mu 0.15 (61.0 at 0.20). Not gamed: no number ranks the design above a better one; the friction claim is a label.
